definitions.definition: ut(x,t)=u_t(x,t)=d/dr u(x,r)|_{r=t}, the time partial derivative. Derivative notation uses the usual total derivative convention (zero if a derivative does not exist); no regularity property is granted by this definition.
utt(x,t)=u_tt(x,t)=d/dr ut(x,r)|_{r=t}, with the same total derivative convention.

definitions.type: family of maps ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m indexed by j∈{1,…,n}
definitions.definition: dxu(j,x,t)=∂_{x_j}u(x,t), the partial derivative in the jth standard coordinate, with the total derivative convention. Further expressions ∂_{x_j}ut and ∂_{x_j}dxu(j,·,t) denote partial derivatives of the displayed functions; the latter is ∂_{x_jx_j}u.
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|²=|ut(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n|dxu(j,x,t)|². Norms are Euclidean; the sum is exactly the Frobenius square |D_xu|², with no factor 1/2.
et(x,t)=e_t(x,t)=d/dr e(x,r)|_{r=t}, with the total derivative convention. Its derivative and integral properties are proved, not part of the definition.

inputs.statement: The functions ut,utt,dxu,e,et are smooth on their stated positive-time domains. For every x∈ℝ^n and r>0, et(x,r)=2ut(x,r)·utt(x,r)+2Σ_{j=1}^n dxu(j,x,r)·∂_{x_j}ut(x,r), and ∂_r dxu(j,x,r)=∂_{x_j}ut(x,r) for each 1≤j≤n. For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable. More precisely, for every τ>0, put J=[τ/2,3τ/2]. There exist a compact C⊂ℝ^n and R>0 such that C⊂(-R,R)^n and u(x,r)=q whenever x∉C and r∈J. Put Q=[-R,R]^n. Its measure is (2R)^n<∞. On (ℝ^n\C)×int J all positive-order derivatives of u vanish. For every r∈int J, the spatial sections of e,et, ut·utt, dxu(j,·,r)·∂_{x_j}ut, ut·∂_{x_j}dxu(j,·,r), and ∂_{x_j}(ut·dxu(j,·,r)), for each 1≤j≤n, are continuous, bounded on Q, zero outside C, and absolutely Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n.

inputs.statement: For a natural k, a family of measure spaces A_i indexed by i∈Fin(k+1), each with sigma-finite volume measure, and an index i₀∈Fin(k+1), the measurable equivalence piFinSuccAbove: (Π_i A_i)→A_i₀×(Π_{j∈Fin k}A_{i₀.succAbove(j)}) preserves volume. It sends x to (x(i₀), j↦x(i₀.succAbove(j))); its inverse inserts the selected coordinate at i₀. On the domain volume is the finite product of all component volumes; on the range it is the product of the selected volume with the remaining finite product volumes. Preservation means measurability and equality of the pushed-forward measure to this range volume.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary spatial index j∈{1,…,n}.
Choose C from N002 for τ=t0.
Choose R jointly with C from N002, with C⊂(-R,R)^n.
I(y,z) has jth coordinate y, and its remaining coordinates, in their original increasing order, are the coordinates of z.
Set Qrest=[-R,R]^k, the box of remaining coordinates.

argument.text:
Fix t0>0 and 1≤j≤n. Choose C,R from N002 for τ=t0 and put Q=[-R,R]^n. Define g(x)=ut(x,t0)·dxu(j,x,t0) and d(x)=∂_{x_j}g(x). H002 makes g smooth. Apply M001 to the j-coordinate sections of its two factors. The product rule gives, for every x∈ℝ^n,
d(x)=∂_{x_j}ut(x,t0)·dxu(j,x,t0)+ut(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}dxu(j,x,t0).
N002 shows g and d vanish outside C, so they vanish on a neighborhood of the boundary of Q: the complement of the closed set C is an open set containing that boundary. The functions g,d and the two displayed summands are continuous with compact support; d and the summands are integrable by N002, and M003 also gives integrability of g.

produces.statement: g and d are smooth, absolutely integrable and zero outside C. For every x∈ℝ^n, d(x)=∂_{x_j}ut(x,t0)·dxu(j,x,t0)+ut(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}dxu(j,x,t0). The two summands are absolutely integrable and vanish outside C, and g vanishes at every boundary point of Q.

argument.text:
Set k=n−1; n=k+1 by H001. Identify ℝ^n with its n real coordinates and define I(y,z) by insertion of y in position j with all remaining coordinates z kept in their original order. Its inverse takes the jth coordinate and the ordered list of other coordinates; these formulas are inverse by inspection coordinate by coordinate. With zero-based indexing i₀=j−1, this inverse is exactly piFinSuccAbove in M011, with all component spaces ℝ. M011 says it preserves product Lebesgue measure, and so does its inverse I. Set Qrest=[-R,R]^k; then I maps [-R,R]×Qrest exactly onto Q. Apply M012 with μ the restriction of real Lebesgue measure to [-R,R], ν the restriction of Lebesgue measure on ℝ^k to Qrest, and integrand (y,z)↦d(I(y,z)). It is continuous and bounded on this compact product and the product measure is finite, hence integrable; equivalently it is the restriction of the integrable compactly supported function d∘I. Change of variables under the measure-preserving coordinate equivalence therefore yields
∫_Q d(x) dx=∫_{Qrest}(∫_{[-R,R]}d(I(y,z)) dy) dz.
For k=0, ℝ^0 is the singleton of empty coordinate lists, whose product volume is one; this formula remains valid.

produces.statement: I maps [-R,R]×Qrest onto Q and preserves the corresponding restricted product Lebesgue measures. Moreover, ∫_Q d(x) dx=∫_{Qrest}(∫_{[-R,R]}d(I(y,z)) dy) dz.

argument.text: For every fixed z∈Qrest, the smooth real function y↦g(I(y,z)) has derivative y↦d(I(y,z)); varying y varies just coordinate j at unit speed. That derivative is continuous, and zero for |y|>R because d is zero outside C⊂int Q. Thus it has compact support in [-R,R], and M003 gives its integrability on ℝ, hence interval integrability on [-R,R]. Apply M007 with endpoints −R,R. Both endpoint values of g(I(±R,z)) are zero by F001, because these points are on the boundary of Q. Hence the interval integral of d(I(y,z)) is zero. The oriented integral from −R to R equals the integral on the closed interval [-R,R], since R>0 and singleton endpoints have Lebesgue measure zero. F002 now gives ∫_Q d=0. Since d is zero outside Q, its integral over ℝ^n is also zero.

Integrate the product formula in F001 and use F003. Its summands are integrable, so linearity gives 0=∫_{ℝ^n}∂_{x_j}ut(x,t0)·dxu(j,x,t0) dx+∫_{ℝ^n}ut(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}dxu(j,x,t0) dx. Symmetry of the real dot product and rearrangement give precisely ∫dxu(j,x,t0)·∂_{x_j}ut(x,t0) dx=−∫ut(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}dxu(j,x,t0) dx. Absolute integrability is part of F001. Arbitrary t0,j give the stated integration-by-parts identity for every positive time and every spatial index.
